raw_case_text:
Case. A 24-year-old patient derived from another center with a diagnosis of delayed healing of left humerus diaphyseal fracture (non-dominant side) with four months of evolution. He had been treated with a brace. At the moment of admission, he had pain and limited motion of his shoulder and elbow. Anteroposterior and lateral radiological images of the humerus showed a line of oblique fracture in the distal third of the diaphysis, and heterogeneous osteolytic and multiloculated images along the entire humerus. The MRI showed pathological images that compromised the entire diaphysis of the humerus and soft tissues at the expansive fracture site, with thinning of the cortical bones. It was decided to perform a biopsy, which resulted in hydatid cysts. The wound of the puncture evolved with the secretion of the hydatids prolonging its healing. Surgical treatment was planned in order to save the limb, given the aggressiveness and expansion of the lesions. Treatment. Oncological resection of the humerus and total replacement of the same with a non-conventional prosthesis designed for the patient was indicated. The surgery was performed using an anteromedial approach extended to the entire diaphysis, achieving total resection. The macroscopic anatomy showed involvement of the entire humerus, including the proximal and distal end with fistulas and vesicles with parasites. The prosthesis at its proximal end consisted of a unipolar head with provisions to attach abductors Fig. 2.
Soft tissue reconstruction was achieved by suturing the divided tendons, i.e., tendons of the rotator cuff, pectoralis major, subscapularis, latissimus dorsi, and teres major, and extensors and flexors in the elbow to the prosthesis. The arm was placed in a sling for six weeks, and the first ROM exercises are started at the elbow. Passive ROM exercises of the shoulder started at four weeks, followed by active exercises at three months and eight weeks after the operation. The patient was also treated with albendazole (15 mg/kg/ d orally) before the operation for one month and after the operation for six months as adjuvant therapy. Result: After two years of follow-up, the patient was pain-free with a range of elbow mobility of 15-90  of flexion-extension, with 0  of pronosupination, and wrist and hand with a full range of motion. At his shoulder he had 30  of anterior flexion, rot ext of 10  and internal rot at the gluteal level.
No local or general disease recurrences were observed. The patient could perform only administrative tasks. The ASES score was 58.33 and Mayo elbow was 65, Quick Dash was 42.3. At present, the patient does not perform tasks or effort with the affected upper limb but can use the hand and the elbow Fig. 3, Fig. 4.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 24-year-old patient presented with a 4-month history of non-healing pathologic left humeral shaft fracture, arm pain, and restricted left shoulder and elbow motion.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient was referred from an outside center after 4 months of brace immobilization for a delayed/non-healing left humeral diaphyseal fracture (non-dominant arm), presenting with persistent pain and restricted shoulder and elbow range of motion. Following incisional biopsy at the referral center, the biopsy puncture tract drained hydatid vesicles.
subjective.past_medical_history: Treated with a functional brace for 4 months prior to referral.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for left arm pain, restricted shoulder/elbow mobility, and post-biopsy hydatid vesicle drainage.

objective.physical_examination: Pain and limited range of motion of the left shoulder and elbow, followed post-biopsy by a draining cutaneous sinus discharging hydatid vesicles.
objective.routine_investigations: Anteroposterior and lateral radiographs of the left humerus demonstrated an oblique fracture in the distal third of the diaphysis accompanied by heterogeneous multiloculated osteolytic lesions spanning the entire humeral shaft.
objective.advanced_workup: Left arm MRI revealed multiloculated cystic lesions compromising the entire humeral diaphysis (from proximal to distal ends) with cortical thinning and surrounding soft-tissue extension. Bone biopsy and subsequent radical en bloc total humeral resection (showing intraosseous vesicles, parasites, and fistulae throughout the entire humerus) confirmed diffuse humeral osseous hydatidosis.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Diffuse intraosseous hydatidosis of the entire left humerus complicated by pathologic diaphyseal fracture and cutaneous fistulization, confirmed by bone biopsy and macroscopic/histopathological examination of the resected humerus. The patient received 1 month of preoperative oral albendazole (15 mg/kg/day), underwent radical total humeral resection and reconstruction with a custom total humerus endoprosthesis and soft-tissue tendon reattachment, and completed 6 months of postoperative albendazole; at 2-year follow-up, he was pain-free and recurrence-free with functional hand/elbow use (ASES 58.33, Mayo Elbow 65, QuickDASH 42.3).
